title: Turk Site, Carlisle County
summary: In Carlisle County, the Turk Site was a small but planned Mississippian town with mounds around a plaza, occupied mainly from about AD 1100 to 1300.
bodyMarkdown:
In Carlisle County, the Turk Site (15Ce6) was a small Mississippian regional center of about 2.5 hectares. Occupied mainly in the Dorena phase (about 1100–1300 CE) and into the Medley phase, it arranged platform mounds around a plaza and may have drawn people from the older Marshall Site (15Ce27), also in Carlisle County. Richard Edging's 1980s work remains the key modern investigation.
Source: [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turk_Site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turk_Site)
